questionText:
The figure shows two 4-tile patterns.

Either one or both of the patterns can be used any number of times and in any orientation to construct a new pattern. Which one of the options below cannot be constructed by using only these two 4-tile patterns assuming there are no overlaps among them?
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze tile divisibility
Both given base patterns consist of exactly $4$ tiles each (a $2 \times 2$ block and a $1 \times 4$ strip). Therefore, any composite structure created without overlaps must have a total number of tiles that is a multiple of $4$.

Step 2: Evaluate each option
• Option (A): Contains a $2 \times 4$ grid = $8$ tiles ($8 = 2 \times 4$, divisible by $4$).
• Option (B): Contains a $3 \times 4$ grid = $12$ tiles ($12 = 3 \times 4$, divisible by $4$).
• Option (C): Contains a $3 \times 5$ grid = $15$ tiles ($15$ is not divisible by $4$).
• Option (D): Contains a $4 \times 4$ grid = $16$ tiles ($16 = 4 \times 4$, divisible by $4$).

Since $15$ tiles cannot be divided into $4$-tile pieces without remainder or overlap, Option (C) cannot be constructed.
